David Hume on experience

David Hume (1711–1776) approaches experience within Empiricism. Causal necessity is a learned expectation, the self is a bundle of perceptions, and moral approval rests in sentiment. Systematically, the teaching links causation, skepticism, sentiment into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets experience most directly—useful for searches such as “david hume quotes on experience.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the David Hume thinker page for biography and to the experience theme for other voices on the same question.
